facts.text: Port Coquitlam's Canadian Pacific rail yard remains B.C.'s largest more than a century after it opened and is still one of the city's top employers.
facts.evidence: The Canadian Pacific Railway relocated its main marshalling yard to Port Coquitlam in 1912 ... The rail yard remains B.C.'s largest more than a century later and is still one of the city's top employers.

facts.text: Port Coquitlam issued 4,605 business licences in 2025, up from 4,420 in 2024.
facts.evidence: The City continued an upward trend for business licences, with 4,605 in 2025 compared to 4,420 in 2024.

facts.text: In 2024, the City of Port Coquitlam approved 500,000 square feet of new industrial and commercial space.
facts.evidence: In 2024, the City approved 500,000 square feet of new industrial/commercial space.

facts.text: Food suppliers Sysco and Lilydale operate significant businesses in Port Coquitlam that move perishable goods to customers quickly.
facts.evidence: Food suppliers Sysco Corp. and Lilydale Inc. are significant businesses in the area that need to move perishable goods to customers quickly.

overview: Port Coquitlam had 61,498 residents in the 2021 Census, up 4.9 percent from 58,612 in 2016, living in 22,884 occupied homes on 29.16 square kilometres. Growth is steady rather than rapid, so most customers are established households who already have favourite suppliers.

The city also has a strong industrial base built around the Canadian Pacific rail yard, food distribution and new industrial space. Businesses here can serve both family households and a sizeable business-to-business market.

byService.seo: Port Coquitlam searchers often add Tri-Cities or Coquitlam to queries, so SEO should cover those terms plus neighbourhoods such as Citadel Heights and Mary Hill without blurring the city name.
byService.website-development: Websites serving Port Coquitlam should load fast on mobile and include a clear business-to-business section, since thousands of licensed businesses, including industrial firms, buy local services here.
byService.branding: Port Coquitlam branding should feel practical and hard-working, matching a city shaped by its rail yard and industry, while staying friendly to the 61,498 residents who shop locally.
